Q1: Triadimefon exhibits known hazards for environmental and oral exposures (Tier 1). An expanded perspective also identifies potential hazards concerning carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, and reproductive health, as well as endocrine disruption, inhalation, dermal, and eye effects (Tier 2). Data for organ and systemic hazards are currently deficient (Tier 4).
Q2: Triadimefon is listed as a chemical of concern, notably on California's Proposition 65 due to its potential to cause cancer, birth defects, or other reproductive harm. It is also recognized on The Endocrine Disruption Exchange (TEDX) list as a potential endocrine disruptor, and is classified as a pesticide active ingredient.
Q3: Triadimefon appears to be extensively studied, supported by over 6,000 literature references, significantly exceeding the median for characterized chemicals. Its well-defined molecular formula and classification as a "Small Molecule" further indicate good characterization, despite one hazard class (organ and systemic effects) currently lacking sufficient data.
